title: What Is Java?
description: Where Java came from, what it is used for, and what makes it strict.

content.value: Java is a programming language, one of the most widely used in the world.

content.real: Sheet music any musician can play
content.concept: A Java program any machine can run
content.text: Java's promise: write your program once, and run it on a Windows laptop, a Mac, a Linux server or an Android phone. The next lesson shows how.

content.question: What is Java's big promise?
options: Write once, run on any machine
content.explain: The same Java program runs on Windows, Mac, Linux and Android without changes.

content.value: Java Is Strict, and That Helps

items: You must say what **kind** of value you store.
Every instruction ends with a semicolon `;`.
If anything is out of place, Java refuses to run at all.
content.title: Java insists

content.real: A spell-checker that blocks sending until you fix a typo
content.concept: Java checking your code before it runs
content.text: Annoying for about a week, then it starts saving you. A misspelled name is an error you see right away, not a crash a user finds later.

output: Every line ends with a semicolon.
content.caption: Forgetting a semicolon is the most common beginner error. If you see `';' expected`, check the end of the line it names.

content.text: Every Java program lives inside a **class** (the outer box). Every instruction lives inside a **method** (the inner box). Curly braces `{ }` mark where each box starts and ends.

content.caption: `class Main` is the class and `main` is the method. Write your instructions between the innermost braces.

content.value: Java calls this way of arranging code **object-oriented**. You will see why it is so powerful in Module 8.

content.question: Where do your instructions go in a Java program?
options: Inside a method, which sits inside a class
content.explain: Instructions live inside a method (like `main`), and the method lives inside a class (like `Main`).

practice.question: Add a third line that prints one place Java is used, for example: Android apps are written in Java. Remember the semicolon.
Delete a semicolon on purpose and press Run. Read the error, then put it back. Getting used to error messages now will save you hours later.

quiz.question: What does every Java instruction end with?
quiz.explain: The semicolon tells Java that the instruction is finished. Leave it out and the compiler keeps reading onto the next line and reports an error.

quiz.question: Why is Java described as strict?
options: It checks your code carefully and refuses to run until mistakes are fixed.
It can only run on one kind of computer.
quiz.explain: Java checks your code before running it. That means you meet your mistakes early, which is far cheaper than meeting them in front of a user.

quiz.question: Where do the instructions of a Java program live?
options: Inside a method, which is inside a class.
Anywhere in the file, in any order.
quiz.explain: Java code is always nested: instructions go in a method, and a method goes in a class. The braces show where each box starts and ends.
